newsitem.title: USA: CME butter deliveries aided by premium to cash.
newsitem.headline: CME butter deliveries aided by premium to cash.

text.p: The large premium that Chicago Mercantile Exchange butter futures recently have held to cash prices resulted in very large deliveries for a new contract that had a small but growing open interest, analysts said.

As of Wednesday, 61 delivery notices had been posted against February butter futures since February 10. The last day for deliveries is February 28. At Tuesday's close, open interest was six contracts. The last trading day was Feb 19.
"There were a lot of people taking advantage of buying the cash and selling the futures and locking in a nice profit," said Mike Downs, dairy analyst with Rosenthal Collins.

Downs said that for most of December and all of January butter futures had run a five to seven cent-per-lb premium over cash butter prices. It only costs about 1-1/2 cents per lb per month to store butter so the profit potential was clear, he said.
"For the most part I think they were all new deliveries," Downs said.
Open interest in February futures at the start of the month was 66 lots. But futures rallied faster than cash in January and February adding to the incentive to deliver.

"Cash butter has moved up aggressively over the past three or four weeks. The price of AA-graded butter jumped 13-1/2 cents on the 14th and 6-1/2 on the seventh of February," said dairy analyst Jerry Dryer.
AA cash butter was quoted at 115.00 cents a lb on Friday, with CME April butter nominally bid at 116.50 cents a lb, unchanged, in Wednesday morning's trade.
"I suspect that the cash market to going to move south (lower) in the next couple of weeks, if not this Friday then next Friday. High prices are cutting off demand," Dryer added.
He said commercial holdings of butter were 21.5 million lbs at end-January, about one week's worth of production. But stocks had risen from just 13.4 million lbs in December.
"So there was a fair bit of inventory building in January," Dryer said.
The CME began trading the new butter contract on September 5, 1996. Each contract calls for delivery of 40,000 lbs of Grade AA butter.
